prose: Nina Shamsi writes about using AI as a writing assistant. She thinks of herself as a bad writer because her pieces wander, and says AI helps her turn a fluid thought process into tidy pieces she can share.

She is unsure the experiment works: she finds AI writing stilted, and says editing it to carry her voice can leave the piece less cohesive than the original draft. She shares her workflow and says she learns the pitfalls by using the tool in different ways. The Lobsters summary adds that AI may amplify weaknesses instead of fixing them.
highlights: Personal account of using AI as a writing assistant
Author sees herself as a wandering writer
AI output feels stilted to her
Editing for voice can reduce cohesion
Shares her process, no feedback available yet
